mainTopic: The סנהדרין's exiles, where witnesses must go, and the nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
overview: The amud finishes the list of places the סנהדרין moved to, ending in טבריה, the lowest of them all. רבי אלעזר counts six exiles from a פסוק, and רבי יוחנן teaches that the redemption will rise from that lowest point. A new משנה teaches that witnesses for the new month go only to the court's meeting place, even if the ראש בית דין is elsewhere. In the גמרא, רב אשי uses this משנה to challenge אמימר, who banned a woman for not following him to מחוזא. אמימר answers that the rule protects only witnesses of the new month, while in a money case 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.' A ברייתא then lists nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, and the ninth is disputed: רב פפא says it was cancelling the כרם רבעי rule, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says it was moving the crimson strip of יום כיפור. Each side challenges the other, and the discussion ends with רב נחמן בר יצחק explaining that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי suggested the strip rule while still a student. That answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rest of the list of places the סנהדרין moved to
steps.stepSummary: The list of the סנהדרין's moves continues: back and forth between יבנה and אושא, then שפרעם, בית שערים, ציפורי, and finally טבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from יבנה to אושא, and from אושא back to יבנה, and from יבנה back to אושא, and from אושא to שפרעם, and from שפרעם to בית שערים, and from בית שערים to ציפורי, and from ציפורי to טבריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started earlier: all the places the סנהדרין had to move to, one after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is a series of moves, not just a list of places. That is why יבנה and אושא show up more than once: the סנהדרין went back and forth between them. The last stop is טבריה.

keyTerms.meaning: Yavne, a town where the סנהדרין sat after leaving ירושלים
Usha, a town in the גליל
Shefaram, a town in the גליל
Tzippori, a major city in the גליל

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the list. It picks up in the middle of a list that began before this section, which is why the first line opens with 'and'.

phrases.english: and from Yavne to Usha, and from Usha to Yavne,
and from Yavne to Usha, and from Usha to Shefaram,
and from Shefaram to Beit She'arim,
and from Beit She'arim to Tzippori,
and from Tzippori to Tiberias.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִיַּבְנֶה לְאוּשָׁא, וּמֵאוּשָׁא לְיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the סנהדרין's moves that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין's journey ended in טבריה, after going back and forth between יבנה and אושא.

steps.title: טבריה is the lowest place, and a פסוק hints at it
steps.stepSummary: טבריה is lower than all the other places, and a פסוק in ישעיהו about being brought low hints at this journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: And טבריה is the lowest of them all, as it says: 'And brought down, you shall speak out of the ground.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last stop, טבריה, is the lowest place of all. It brings a פסוק as a hint to this downward path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each move took the סנהדרין further down, both in where it was and in its standing. The פסוק about being 'brought down' and speaking 'from the ground' fits this path that ends in the lowest place.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, the last stop of the סנהדרין
and you will be brought low

phrases.english: And Tiberias is the lowest of them all,
as it says: "And brought down, you shall speak out of the ground."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּטְבֶרְיָא עֲמוּקָּה מִכּוּלָּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the last stop in the list and brings a פסוק as a hint.
steps.raayaObject: That the סנהדרין's path went downward and ended in the lowest place, טבריה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 29:4, 'And brought down, you shall speak out of the ground.'

steps.title: רבי אלעזר counts six exiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says there were six exiles and learns it from a פסוק with six words of lowering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: There are six exiles, as it says: 'For He has brought down those who dwell high, the lofty city; He lays it low, lays it low to the ground, brings it to the dust.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a different count: six exiles, not a count of every single move. He uses a different פסוק to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full list counts every trip, even the repeat trips between יבנה and אושא. רבי אלעזר instead counts places rather than trips. The גמרא does not spell out which six places he means. The פסוק has six words of lowering to match.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: six exiles,
as it says: "For He has brought down those who dwell high,"
the lofty city, He lays it low,
lays it low to the ground,
brings it to the dust."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: שֵׁשׁ גָּלוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second way to count the exiles, with a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין went through six exiles, matching six words of lowering in ישעיהו 26:5.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the redemption will come from the lowest point
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the future redemption will begin from that lowest place, as the פסוק says 'Shake yourself from the dust.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: And from there they are destined to be redeemed, as it says: 'Shake yourself from the dust, arise, sit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן ends the topic on a hopeful note. The same low place the סנהדרין reached is where the redemption will start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last word of רבי אלעזר's פסוק was 'dust.' רבי יוחנן brings a פסוק that starts with rising up from the dust. So the lowest point becomes the starting point of the redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: they are destined to, in the future

steps.whatToRemember: The סנהדרין went down step by step until טבריה, the lowest place. רבי יוחנן teaches that the redemption will rise from that very place.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And from there they are destined to be redeemed,
phrases.notes: 'From there' means from the lowest place they reached, טבריה.

phrases.english: as it says: "Shake yourself from the dust, arise, sit."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּמִשָּׁם עֲתִידִין לִיגָּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing thought to the exile discussion: the redemption will come from the lowest point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The future redemption will begin from the place where the סנהדרין's exile ended.

steps.title: משנה: Witnesses go to the court's meeting place, not to the ראש בית דין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה reports another תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: even if the ראש בית דין is somewhere else, witnesses go only to the place where the court meets.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said: And רבן יוחנן בן זכאי also made this rule: even if the head of the court is in some other place, the witnesses should go only to the place where the court gathers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches one more rule made by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי about witnesses who come to report the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the witnesses should go to wherever the ראש בית דין is, since he is the one who declares the new month. This תקנה says no: they go to the court's regular meeting place. The court there can declare the month even without the head.

keyTerms.meaning: the place where the court gathers

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה becomes the source for the story right after it, about whether a person must follow a judge who travels.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: Mishnah: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד זֹאת הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: And this, too, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: that even if the head of the court is in any other place,
the witnesses should not go
anywhere except to the place where the court gathers.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה: וְעוֹד זֹאת הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic: where the witnesses for the new moon must go.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses go only to the court's meeting place, even if the ראש בית דין is elsewhere.

steps.title: The story: אמימר puts a woman under a ban
steps.stepSummary: A woman was called to court before אמימר in נהרדעא. אמימר went to מחוזא, she did not follow him there, and he wrote a ban against her.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A certain woman was summoned to judgment before אמימר in נהרדעא. אמימר went to מחוזא, and she did not go after him. He wrote a document of excommunication against her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that connects to the משנה. It sets up the question of whether a person must follow a judge who travels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר treated the woman as someone who refused to come to court, because she did not follow him to his new location. The question is whether the court is wherever the judge is, or only the court's regular place.

phrases.english: Gemara: There was a certain woman
who was summoned to judgment
before Ameimar in Neharde'a.
Ameimar went to Mechoza,
and she did not go after him.
He wrote a document of excommunication against her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא אִיתְּתָא דְּאַזְמְנוּהָ לְדִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַמֵּימָר בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמימר acted as if a person must follow the judge to wherever he goes.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges אמימר from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר: our משנה says people go only to the court's meeting place, not to wherever the ראש בית דין is. So why put her under a ban?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But didn't we learn in the משנה: Even if the head of the court is in any other place, the witnesses should go only to the place where the court gathers!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges what אמימר did, using the משנה we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the obligation is to go to the court's place, not to follow the judge. The woman's case was set in נהרדעא, so she should not have had to go to מחוזא. The ban looks unjustified.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (in a משנה)? — a challenge formula

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: Even if the head of the court is in any other place,
the witnesses should not go
anywhere except to the place where the court gathers!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר, וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's action in the story, using the rule of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ban on the woman for not following him to מחוזא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says people go to the court's meeting place, not to wherever the ראש בית דין is. So she had no duty to follow אמימר to מחוזא, and the ban looks wrong.

steps.title: אמימר explains why the woman had to follow him
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the 'meeting place only' rule is only for witnesses of the new month. In a money case, the defendant must go where the court is.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said to him: That rule is only about testimony for the new month. If we made those witnesses travel, they would not want to come next time. But here, in a money case, 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.'
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי's question from step 7. He limits the rule of the משנה to עדות החודש only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that witnesses go only to the court's fixed place exists to protect witnesses of the new month. If they were sent chasing after the ראש בית דין, they might not come again in the future. A defendant in a money case has no such protection, because the פסוק teaches that the borrower must serve the lender. So she had to follow the court to מחוזא, and the ban was justified.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only to a certain case)
Testimony about seeing the new moon
Making them stumble in the future, so they will not come again
The borrower is a servant to the lender

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same practical question (where must people go?) can have different answers depending on the reason behind the rule.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אמימר answering רב אשי.

phrases.english: These words apply only to testimony about the new month,
because if so, you would end up
making them stumble in the future.
phrases.notes: He means that if witnesses are made to travel around, they might not bother coming next time.

phrases.english: But here,
"The borrower is a servant to the lender."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְעִנְיַן עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question by limiting the scope of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to its original case (עדות החודש only).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי thought the rule 'go only to the meeting place' applied to all court matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule protects only witnesses of the new month. In money cases, the defendant must follow the court.

steps.title: No sandals on the platform, and the count of nine enactments
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in sandals. This is one of nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: six are in this perek and one is in the first perek.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: כהנים may not go up to the platform in their sandals. This is one of the nine enactments that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made. Six are in this chapter, and one is in the first chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a תקנה for כהנים. That ברייתא says there are nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, so the גמרא starts counting where they are found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sandal rule is added to the list of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות. The גמרא counts seven so far: six from this perek and one from the first perek. This sets up the next steps, which will name the remaining two.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform where כהנים stand to say ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Kohanim are not allowed
to go up in their sandals to the platform,
and this is one of the nine enactments
that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted.
Six are in this chapter,
and one is in the first chapter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין כֹּהֲנִים רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲלוֹת בְּסַנְדְּלֵיהֶן לַדּוּכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the court-location topic to a list of all of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים may not go up to the דוכן in sandals. This is one of nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

steps.title: The eighth enactment: a convert's bird-offering money
steps.stepSummary: The eighth תקנה is about a convert today setting aside a quarter-shekel for his bird offering. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says רבן יוחנן cancelled it because of the risk of a mishap.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one is from a ברייתא: A person who converts nowadays must set aside a quarter for his pair of birds. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: רבן יוחנן already took a vote and cancelled it, because of the risk of a mishap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the eighth תקנה. It is about a convert's bird offering, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה here was to cancel the old practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the בית המקדש, a convert used to put aside money for his future bird offering. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cancelled this practice because the money could be misused by mistake. So the תקנה here is the cancellation itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'nest': a pair of birds brought as an offering

steps.confusionAlert: Here the תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is not a new obligation. He cancelled the earlier practice of setting money aside.

phrases.english: And the other one, as was taught:
A convert who converts at this time,
must set aside a quarter for his nest.
phrases.notes: His 'nest' is his pair of birds for the offering, and the 'quarter' is a quarter-shekel to pay for them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר נִמְנָה עָלֶיהָ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן וּבִיטְּלָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan already took a vote on it and cancelled it,
because of the mishap.
phrases.notes: The worry is that someone might use the set-aside money by mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the count of nine תקנות by naming the eighth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cancelled the practice of a convert setting aside a quarter-shekel for his offering, because of the risk of misuse.

steps.title: The ninth enactment is disputed
steps.stepSummary: The ninth תקנה is a מחלוקת. רב פפא says it is about כרם רבעי, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is about the strip of crimson wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one is a dispute between רב פפא and רב נחמן בר יצחק. רב פפא said: a fourth-year vineyard. רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the strip of crimson wool.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the ninth and last תקנה. The אמוראים disagree about which one it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the list of nine. Since the תקנה is disputed, there are two possible candidates, כרם רבעי or the לשון של זהורית. The next steps explain each one: כרם רבעי in step 12 and the crimson strip in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: A vineyard in its fourth year, whose fruit has special holiness

steps.whatToRemember: There are nine תקנות of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: six in this perek, one in the first perek, the convert's bird money (which he cancelled), and a ninth that is disputed (כרם רבעי or the crimson strip).

phrases.english: And the other one is a dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב פָּפָּא וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: between Rav Pappa and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.
Rav Pappa said: a fourth-year vineyard,

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: the strip of crimson wool.
phrases.notes: Each view is explained in the next steps: כרם רבעי first, then the crimson strip.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב פָּפָּא וְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the ninth and final תקנה, completing the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ninth תקנה is disputed: כרם רבעי according to רב פפא, or the לשון של זהורית according to רב נחמן בר יצחק.

steps.title: רב פפא: the fourth-year vineyard rule and its borders
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the ninth תקנה is about כרם רבעי. He brings a ברייתא: fruit grown within a day's walk of ירושלים had to be brought there, and the ברייתא lists the borders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it is the fourth-year vineyard, as it was taught: the fruit of a fourth-year vineyard would go up to ירושלים from a day's walk in every direction. These are the borders: אילת in the north, עקרבת in the south, לוד in the west, and the ירדן in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the first opinion from step 11. It brings the old rule that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי later changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually fruit of a כרם רבעי can be redeemed for money, and the money is brought to ירושלים. But for vineyards close to ירושלים, a day's walk away or less, the fruit itself had to be carried there. The ברייתא marks that area with four border points.

keyTerms.meaning: A vineyard in its fourth year. Its fruit is holy and is eaten in ירושלים
Its border, the edge of the area

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: it is the fourth-year vineyard,
as it was taught: a fourth-year vineyard
would go up to Jerusalem
phrases.notes: This means the actual fruit had to be brought. It could not be swapped for money.

phrases.english: from a day's walk in every direction,
and this is its border:
Eilat in the north,
and Akrabat in the south,
Lod in the west,
and the Jordan in the east.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion about the ninth תקנה from step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit of a כרם רבעי within a day's walk of ירושלים had to be brought there itself, inside the borders of Eilat, Akrabat, Lod and the Jordan.

steps.title: The reason: to fill Jerusalem's markets with fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains why the fruit had to be brought: so the markets of ירושלים would be full of fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say רבה בר עולא said, in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is the reason? To decorate the markets of ירושלים with fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind the rule from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was meant to keep ירושלים full of fruit. This reason matters, because once the reason is gone, the rule can be cancelled. The story in steps 14-15 shows that this happened.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason explains why the rule could later be cancelled after the בית המקדש was destroyed.

phrases.english: And Ulla said,
and some say it was Rabba bar Ulla,
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
What is the reason?
In order to decorate the markets of Jerusalem with fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מָה טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rule taught in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fruit had to be brought so that the markets of ירושלים would be full of fruit.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר wants to give his vineyard away to the poor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבי אליעזר had a כרם רבעי east of לוד, inside the border, and wanted to make it ownerless for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר had a fourth-year vineyard east of לוד, next to כפר טבי. רבי אליעזר wanted to make it ownerless for the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story to show how the כרם רבעי rule was later cancelled. This step sets up the students' answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: East of לוד is inside the border, because לוד is the western edge. So רבי אליעזר thought he still had to bring the fruit to ירושלים. Since that was hard for him, he planned to give it up and let the poor take it.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it ownerless, so anyone may take it
The village of Tavi, near לוד

phrases.english: And it was taught: a fourth-year vineyard
belonged to Rabbi Eliezer,
east of Lod, beside the village of Tavi,
and Rabbi Eliezer wanted
to make it ownerless for the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that will show the rule from steps 12-13 was cancelled
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר, whose כרם רבעי was inside the border, planned to make it ownerless for the poor.

steps.title: The students: your colleagues already permitted it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's students tell him there is no need. His colleagues already voted and permitted redeeming the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, your colleagues already took a vote on it and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The students tell רבי אליעזר that the old rule is no longer in force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים voted to cancel the requirement to bring the actual fruit. Now the fruit can be redeemed even close to ירושלים. So רבי אליעזר does not need to give up his vineyard.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Rabbi,
your colleagues have already voted on it
and permitted it.
phrases.notes: They permitted redeeming the fruit, so it no longer has to be carried to ירושלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, כְּבָר נִמְנוּ חֲבֵרֶיךָ עָלָיו וְהִתִּירוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי אליעזר's plan in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים voted to cancel the rule requiring the fruit itself to be brought to ירושלים.

steps.title: The colleagues were רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who these colleagues were and answers: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. This shows the cancellation was his תקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are 'your colleagues'? רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the leader of the vote. This closes the proof that this is one of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's nine תקנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of the story is to connect the cancellation to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. Once we know he led it, רב פפא's view is explained: the ninth תקנה is cancelling the כרם רבעי rule.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the ninth תקנה was cancelling the rule that כרם רבעי fruit near ירושלים must be brought there. The reason for the rule was to fill the markets of ירושלים, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי led the vote to cancel it.

phrases.english: Who are "your colleagues"?
Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חֲבֵרֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the colleagues mentioned in step 15, linking the story to step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The cancellation of the כרם רבעי rule was done by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, so it counts as his ninth תקנה according to רב פפא.

steps.title: The ninth ordinance was about the crimson strip
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ninth תקנה was about the לשון של זהורית. He brings a ברייתא: at first the strip was tied outside the אולם, then it was moved inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the ordinance was about the crimson strip. A ברייתא teaches: at first they tied it on the outside of the door of the אולם. If it turned white, people were happy. If not, they were sad. So they ruled to tie it on the inside of the door.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different answer than רב פפא about which ordinance was the ninth. He starts a ברייתא that describes how the crimson strip was moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור a crimson strip turning white was a sign that the people were forgiven. When it stayed red, everyone could see it and was upset. So the חכמים moved it inside, where fewer people could see it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Entrance Hall of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
[The ordinance was about] the strip of crimson wool,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ קוֹשְׁרִין לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית
phrases.english: At first they would tie a strip of crimson wool
on the doorway of the Entrance Hall, on the outside.
If it turned white, they would rejoice;
if it did not turn white, they would be sad.
They instituted that they should tie it
on the doorway of the Entrance Hall, on the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion about the ninth תקנה from step 11, after רב פפא's view was explained in steps 12-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ninth תקנה concerned the crimson strip of יום כיפור.

steps.title: People still peeked, so the strip was moved to the goat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: people still peeked inside. So the strip was tied half on a rock and half between the horns of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But people still peeked and saw. If it turned white they were happy, and if not they were sad. So they ruled to tie half of it on the rock and half between the horns of the goat that was sent away.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its story. Since moving the strip inside did not stop people from looking, the חכמים moved it to a place no one in the crowd could see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was the people's sadness when the strip stayed red. The final fix was to tie the strip out with the שעיר המשתלח, far from the crowd. According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, this is the תקנה being counted.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away on יום כיפור (the scapegoat)

steps.whatToRemember: In רב נחמן בר יצחק's view, the ninth תקנה was moving the crimson strip so that people would not be upset on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: But they would still peek and see;
if it turned white, they would rejoice;
if it did not turn white, they would be sad.
They instituted that they should tie it,
half of it to the rock

phrases.aramaic: וְחֶצְיוֹ בֵּין קַרְנָיו שֶׁל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ.
phrases.english: and half of it between the horns of the scapegoat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲדַיִין הָיוּ מְצִיצִין וְרוֹאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The final arrangement was to tie half the strip to the rock and half to the scapegoat's horns.

steps.title: Why didn't רב נחמן בר יצחק agree with רב פפא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן בר יצחק did not accept רב פפא's answer about כרם רבעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason that רב נחמן בר יצחק did not say like רב פפא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the two opinions. Here it sets up the next move by asking what was wrong, in רב נחמן בר יצחק's eyes, with רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had a good proof: the story of רבי אליעזר and the students' words 'your colleagues'. So the גמרא wants to know what problem רב נחמן בר יצחק saw in it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַאי טַעְמָא
phrases.english: What is the reason that Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak
did not say like Rav Pappa?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from presenting the two views to examining why they disagree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness did רב נחמן בר יצחק see in רב פפא's identification?

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's teacher, not his colleague
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק would argue that the students said 'your colleagues', but רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: if you think it was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, was he רבי אליעזר's colleague? He was his teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב נחמן בר יצחק. The word 'colleagues' does not fit רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the students said that רבי אליעזר's colleagues had permitted redeeming the fruit. But רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's רבי. So the story cannot be about him, and רב פפא's proof falls apart.

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: If you think it was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
was he one of Rabbi Eliezer's colleagues?
He was his teacher!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, חֲבֵרָיו דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'colleagues' cannot refer to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who was רבי אליעזר's teacher.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's proof from the story of רבי אליעזר's כרם רבעי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The students' wording 'your colleagues' does not fit a teacher.

steps.title: Students would not say 'your teacher' to their teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's defense: the students were speaking to their own teacher, and it would be disrespectful to call someone 'your teacher' in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Since they were students, it is not proper manners to say to one's teacher 'your teacher.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב פפא's reply. The students chose the word 'colleagues' out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא agrees that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's teacher. But the students were talking to רבי אליעזר, who was their own רבי. Saying 'your teacher' to him would sound like it made him smaller, so they said 'colleagues' instead. This keeps רב פפא's proof standing.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (what does he answer?)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is רב פפא. How does he deal with this problem?

phrases.english: Since they were students,
it is not proper manners
for one to say to his teacher, "your teacher."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? כֵּיוָן דְּתַלְמִידִים הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב פפא against the objection of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the wording as a matter of respectful speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Colleagues' must mean people of the same rank as רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The students said 'colleagues' out of respect, even though they meant his teacher.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not deny that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was רבי אליעזר's teacher. He only explains why the students did not say so.

steps.title: Why didn't רב פפא agree with רב נחמן בר יצחק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the mirror question: why didn't רב פפא accept the crimson strip as the ninth תקנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason that רב פפא did not say like רב נחמן בר יצחק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. It sets up the next move by asking what problem רב פפא saw in the crimson strip answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view has to explain why it rejects the other. Now the גמרא looks for רב פפא's objection.

phrases.english: And what is the reason that Rav Pappa

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק?
phrases.english: did not say like Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב פָּפָּא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror of step 19, now aimed at רב פפא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness did רב פפא see in the crimson strip identification?

steps.title: Did the crimson strip still turn white in רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's time?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא would argue that the crimson strip may no longer have turned white in the years when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled and made תקנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: if you think it was רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, was there a crimson strip in the days of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב פפא with a timing problem. It suggests the crimson strip no longer turned white during the years when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled and made תקנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the strip no longer turned white, there was no joy or sadness to hide, so רבן יוחנן בן זכאי would have had no reason to make a rule about where to tie it. This question is the setup. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A title of honor for the head of the חכמים

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי —
phrases.english: If you think it was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
in the days of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
was there a strip of crimson wool?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי — בִּימֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מִי הֲוָה לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crimson strip apparently no longer turned white in the years when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled and made תקנות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's identification of the ninth תקנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule about the strip's placement cannot come from someone who ruled when the strip no longer turned white.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's 120 years
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא begins his proof with a ברייתא that splits רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's 120-year life into three periods of forty years.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: all the years of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי were 120. Forty years he did business, forty years he learned, and forty years he taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to lay out the timeline of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's life. This sets up a proof about when he led the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was a teacher and leader only in his last forty years. This timeline is the first piece of רב פפא's proof that the crimson strip no longer turned white by then. The rest of the proof comes in steps 25 and 26.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: All the years of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
were one hundred and twenty years.
Forty years he was involved in business,
forty years he learned,
forty years he taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כׇּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first source supporting רב פפא's timing objection in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that the crimson strip no longer turned white in the years when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא dividing רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's 120 years into business, learning, and teaching

steps.title: The crimson strip stopped turning white forty years before the destruction
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings a ברייתא: in the last forty years before the בית המקדש was destroyed, the crimson strip no longer turned white. It turned red instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: during the forty years before the בית המקדש was destroyed, the crimson strip did not turn white. It turned red instead.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings the second piece of his proof. It is a ברייתא that dates the crimson strip to a specific period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those last forty years the strip never turned white, so there was no joy or sadness to hide, and no reason to move it. The תקנות about where to tie the strip must therefore come from before those forty years. That earlier time was before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's years of making תקנות.

phrases.english: And it is taught in a ברייתא: forty years
before the Temple was destroyed

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית מַלְבִּין
phrases.english: the strip of crimson wool would not turn white
rather, it would turn red.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁנֶּחֱרַב הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof begun in step 24 by giving a time marker for the crimson strip.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that the crimson strip practice does not belong to the period when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made his תקנות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the crimson strip during the forty years before the destruction.

steps.title: His תקנות came only after the destruction
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made his תקנות after the destruction. Since the strip had already stopped turning white forty years before the destruction, a rule about where to tie it must come from an earlier stage of his life, when he was not yet making תקנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in the משנה: once the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made his תקנות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא closes his proof by quoting our משנה, which places רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות after the destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made his תקנות after the destruction. The step before showed that the strip תקנות came before the last forty years of the בית המקדש, which was long before that time. So רב פפא concludes the strip rule was made while he was still a student, and it cannot be counted among his תקנות.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's view: the crimson strip comes from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's student years, and his תקנות came only after the destruction. So it is not counted as his ninth תקנה.

phrases.english: And we learned in the משנה: when the Temple was destroyed
Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted his ordinances!
phrases.notes: This is from our own משנה. It shows his תקנות came after the destruction, not before.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: מִשֶּׁחָרַב הַבַּיִת הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by placing the crimson strip in his student years, which came before his years of making תקנות.
steps.raayaObject: That the crimson strip practice is not one of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה stating that he made his תקנות after the destruction.

steps.title: How would the other אמורא answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן בר יצחק, who does count the crimson strip, would answer רב פפא's proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, how would he answer?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא turns to רב נחמן בר יצחק to hear how he deals with רב פפא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא showed that the crimson strip came during רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's student years. If so, how can רב נחמן בר יצחק count it among his תקנות? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other (opinion), what would he say?

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: This means רב נחמן בר יצחק, who counted the crimson strip as the ninth תקנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the proof just completed into a challenge for רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רב נחמן בר יצחק explains counting the crimson strip if it came during רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's student years.

steps.title: He suggested it while still a student
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers: during the forty years that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was learning, he suggested this practice in front of his teacher, and his reasoning was accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: During those forty years that he was learning, he was a student sitting before his teacher. He said an idea, and his reasoning made sense to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer: even a student can suggest a rule that gets adopted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק agrees that the crimson strip comes from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's student years. But he says that does not stop it from being his idea. He proposed it, and the חכמים accepted his reasoning, so it can still be credited to him.

keyTerms.meaning: That he learned (his years of study)
A student sitting before his teacher

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not saying the timing is wrong. He accepts that this was during the student years. He only argues that an idea from a student can still be credited to him.

phrases.english: Those forty years that he studied
he was a student sitting before his teacher
and he said a matter, and his reasoning made sense.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָם אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה דְּלָמַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 on behalf of רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crimson strip practice was suggested by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי as a student. His reasoning was accepted, so it can still be counted as his.
